info.name: Modernizing Enterprise Applications — Behavior-Equivalence Suite
info.description: The behavior-equivalence suite (r02-plan S6, notification-plan S2, inventory-plan S2, payment-plan S2, build-plan.md §G/§D). Captured against the running Spring Boot monolith (examples/00-monolith). This collection is the project's equivalence gate: it is re-run UNCHANGED against each extracted service (starting with the Quarkus Review service, ch.15) and a service is only considered 'done' once it passes this same suite with no edits (build-plan.md §G load-bearing rule). Every request targets {{baseUrl}} so the identical collection can point at the monolith or at an extracted service's own port. Covers: (1) happy-path checkout — ADAPTED for the forthcoming ASYNC checkout contract (payment-plan.md S2, DRQ-047/DRQ-055): the POST is tolerant of `201` (today's synchronous monolith) or `202` (the future choreographed-saga payment service), and a BOUNDED-WAIT poll of GET /api/orders/{id} asserts the order strictly reaches the terminal `CONFIRMED` status — only the transport is relaxed, the terminal outcome and the stock-decrement side effect are unchanged and strict; (2) out-of-stock — left untouched/fully synchronous (inventory Reserve stays synchronous even after the payment extraction, so POST still returns `409` immediately); (3) payment-declined — ADAPTED the same way (DRQ-047/DRQ-055): POST tolerant of `402` (today's synchronous monolith — the whole checkout transaction is rolled back/compensated before the response, so there is no order to poll) or `202` (the saga — order persists PENDING, decline arrives later), then a BOUNDED-WAIT poll of GET /api/orders/{id} strictly asserting `PAYMENT_DECLINED` (saga path only) AND a BOUNDED-WAIT poll of GET /api/inventory/{sku} strictly asserting stock returns to net-zero (both paths) — the crux assertion (compensation via an in-line Release today, via the payment.declined choreography reaction later, DRQ-049) is never weakened; (4) the Review context contract (list, get-by-id, unauthenticated POST -> 401, authenticated POST -> 201, validation -> 400) — the first extraction's externally-observable surface — (5) the Notification context contract (DRQ-037): a checkout followed by a BOUNDED-WAIT poll of GET /api/notifications?customerId= so the identical assertion is correct whether the order-confirmation notification is written synchronously in-transaction (today's monolith, hits on the first attempt) or eventually via outbox -> Kafka -> consumer (the future async notification service, ch.17) — and (6) the Inventory Context Contract (inventory-plan.md S2, DRQ-046): the `/api/inventory` READ surface (list + get-by-sku + 404 for an unknown sku), asserted as a synchronous request/response (no bounded-wait — Reserve stays synchronous, DRQ-041) — distinct from, and NOT a duplicate of, the cross-seam inventory-mutation behavior already proven by Scenario 1 (stock decrements by ordered qty), Scenario 2 (out-of-stock -> 409, stock unchanged) and Scenario 3 (payment-declined -> stock rolled back, not left decremented), which remain the load-bearing inventory-equivalence checks the ch.19/ch.23 extractions must keep green across the seam — and (7) the Payment Context Contract (payment-plan.md S2b, DRQ-055), added after an S8 cutover run found it missing from S2's delivery: the `/api/payments` READ surface (list by orderId + get-by-id, PaymentDto-shaped), correlated with Scenario 1's confirmed order (reusing `happyPathOrderId`) so a CAPTURED payment row is guaranteed in both the synchronous-monolith and choreographed-saga states — plus the Notification Context Contract's checkout step (formerly 5a), which S8 also found still asserting the stale synchronous 201/CONFIRMED contract; it is now adapted to the same 201|202-tolerant, bounded-wait-to-CONFIRMED pattern as Scenario 1's 1b/1c before the downstream notification check runs; (8) Scenario 4 — Shipping-Failure (shipping-plan.md S2, ch.24, DRQ-059/060/062/065 — the H2/H3 crux): a checkout carrying the deterministic `SHIP-FAIL` sentinel in `shippingAddress` (DRQ-062, the shipping analogue of payment's `CARD-DECLINE`), then a BOUNDED-WAIT poll of GET /api/orders/{id} strictly asserting the terminal `SHIPPING_FAILED` status AND a BOUNDED-WAIT poll of GET /api/inventory/{sku} strictly asserting stock returns to net-zero — the orchestrated, coordinator-initiated, cross-context compensation (DRQ-060) this scenario exists to prove genuinely fires. Today's in-process monolith has no shipping-failure path at all, so this scenario is honestly gated PENDING at baseline (a `shippingSagaEnabled` collection variable, default `false`, plus a `setNextRequest` skip guard — NOT Postman's `disabled` flag, which newman's CLI runner does not honor) and is enabled for real at S8 cutover; and (9) the Shipping Context Contract (shipping-plan.md S2, DRQ-063): the `/api/shipments` READ surface (list by orderId + get-by-id + 404 on an unknown id, ShipmentDto-shaped: id/orderId/address/status/createdAt), correlated with Scenario 1's confirmed order — this folder asserts only the read contract, never a mode-specific status, so it is green both before and after the shipping cutover.

SF-gate. Shipping-failure scenario gate — PENDING at baseline until S8 cutover

request.description: BASELINE/HONESTY GUARD (shipping-plan S2, HARD PART H2). Today's in-process monolith has NO shipping-failure path — OrderSagaListener#onPaymentCaptured always confirms + dispatches (ShippingService#dispatch never fails) — so this whole scenario cannot pass against it. Rather than relying on Postman's per-item `disabled: true` flag (VERIFIED by hand against newman 6.2.2: the CLI runner does NOT honor `disabled` — it still executes the item — so `disabled: true` alone would make this folder run-and-fail the baseline), this item is a cheap, harmless, always-true reachability check whose test script is the REAL gate: it inspects the `shippingSagaEnabled` collection variable (default `false`) and, when disabled, calls `postman.setNextRequest('4a. List reviews by sku -> 200, array')` to jump straight past SF-a..SF-d — so the actual SHIP-FAIL order placement and its SHIPPING_FAILED/net-zero assertions never execute at baseline (they cannot falsely pass OR falsely fail an unexercised path). Flip `shippingSagaEnabled` to `true` at S8 (shipping.mode=orchestrated, strangler.shipping.enabled=true) to enable this scenario for real.

request.description: SENTINEL CHOICE (DRQ-062, documented here per shipping-plan S2): the `SHIP-FAIL` marker goes in `shippingAddress`, NOT a sentinel sku. DRQ-059's saga sequence is enrich (fetch the order's address from the order read surface) -> dispatch shipment -> book carrier (the deterministic SHIP-FAIL throw point) -> emit; the address is the one field the saga already reads for enrichment, so an exact-match sentinel there is the most direct analogue to payment's exact-match `paymentMethod: "CARD-DECLINE"` (DRQ-048) — a sentinel sku would require the book-carrier step to additionally inspect order line items, which DRQ-059's sequence gives it no documented reason to do. `shippingAddress` is set to the exact value `SHIP-FAIL` (mirroring `CARD-DECLINE`'s exact-match convention). This request only runs when `shippingSagaEnabled=true` (post S8 cutover) — see SF-gate.

item.name: 5c. Confirmation notification becomes observable (bounded-wait poll)

exec: // DRQ-037 bounded-wait eventual-consistency poll: only delay on a RETRY
// (attempts > 0), never on the first attempt. Against today's synchronous
// monolith the notification is already there on attempt 0, so this never
// sleeps and the folder passes immediately. Against the future async
// service (outbox -> Kafka -> SmallRye consumer) this gives each retry a
// short, bounded window for the event to be consumed. A plain busy-wait is
// used (not setTimeout) so the delay is honored identically by the Postman
// app and by newman's non-interactive sandbox before the request is sent.
while (Date.now() - start < delayMs) { /* intentional bounded busy-wait */ }
// Not observable yet and the retry budget is not exhausted: this is the
// ONLY branch that loops. Correct for BOTH backends — a synchronous

// Either found, or the bounded-wait budget is exhausted: assert the
